title: One-Batch Taqueria Salsas
summary: One fresh tomato salsa turned into three more: finer, cooked taquera-style, and a creamy avocado version.
difficulty_reason: Blend, simmer, chop; the variations are simple add-ins.

ingredients.line: 2 jalapeños, chopped (more or fewer to taste)
2 tsp salt, pepper and garlic seasoning
A handful of cilantro, finely chopped

steps: Quarter the tomatoes and chop the jalapeños, onion and cilantro. Add them to a blender with the garlic and seasoning.
Blend to a chunky texture for salsa #1, the fresh salsa. Taste and adjust the seasoning and heat.
Return part of the salsa to the blender and blend until fine, for a smoother base.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a stainless steel pan over medium heat, until hot but not smoking.
Pour in the fine salsa and whisk it into the oil, then simmer about 10 minutes, until deeper in color and thick, for salsa #2, the taquera.
Dress up salsa #2: stir in diced onion, chopped cilantro and cubed avocado to make salsa #3.
For salsa #4, the creamy taqueria-style salsa, blend the hot taquera salsa with extra oil until it turns creamy and rich.
tips: Quantities are flexible; use more tomatoes for a milder salsa, more peppers for heat.
Cooking the blended salsa in oil gives it the deep flavor of a taqueria salsa.
